root_cause.text: In virtio_net, `struct virtnet_info` embedded `struct virtio_net_rss_config_trailer` with a flexible array member before `rss_hash_key_data`, so tail padding in the trailer caused `rss_trailer.hash_key_data` and `rss_hash_key_data` to have different offsets and the RSS key buffer to be read/written one byte off.
root_cause.evidence: The commit states `rss_trailer.hash_key_data` was at offset 83 while `rss_hash_key_data` was at offset 84 because `struct virtio_net_rss_config_trailer` had 1 byte of padding, causing “the RSS key passed to the device [to be] shifted by 1 byte,” and fixes it by using `TRAILING_OVERLAP()` plus a `static_assert` that both offsets are equal.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove RSS configuration storage from virtnet_info to shift or eliminate that per-device state without altering the surrounding interface.
intent_record.what: Three RSS-related fields were removed from struct virtnet_info: the pointer rss_hdr, the embedded rss_trailer structure, and the rss_hash_key_data byte array.
intent_record.how: At runtime, instances of virtnet_info no longer allocate or retain these RSS configuration members, reducing per-device state and indicating that this RSS data is no longer stored directly in the main device structure and is expected to be handled elsewhere.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add embedded RSS config header/trailer storage with compile-time layout validation so virtio-net can safely manage RSS hash key data.
intent_record.what: The struct virtnet_info is extended with a new pointer field rss_hdr of type struct virtio_net_rss_config_hdr *, and a new trailing-overlap field rss_trailer is added using TRAILING_OVERLAP around struct virtio_net_rss_config_trailer with an overlapping u8 rss_hash_key_data[VIRTIO_NET_RSS_MAX_KEY_SIZE] buffer. A static_assert is also added to verify that offsetof(struct virtnet_info, rss_trailer.hash_key_data) matches offsetof(struct virtnet_info, rss_hash_key_data).
intent_record.how: At runtime this changes the layout of virtnet_info so it can hold RSS configuration header/trailer data while reusing the same memory region for the trailer's flexible-array hash key storage through a fixed-size in-struct buffer. The static assertion prevents layout mismatches at build time, ensuring code can safely access the hash key data via either view without corrupting memory.

Add embedded RSS config header/trailer storage with compile-time layout validation so virtio-net can safely manage RSS hash key data.

relevance_review.reason: The root cause is the incorrect embedding/layout of RSS configuration data inside struct virtnet_info, specifically involving the trailer and hash key storage. Removing RSS configuration storage from virtnet_info directly addresses that faulty in-struct layout and thus is related to the vulnerability.

The change directly addresses the RSS config header/trailer layout and adds compile-time validation to ensure the embedded trailer and RSS hash key data have the correct offsets, which matches the root cause of the one-byte misalignment caused by tail padding around the flexible array member.

candidates.rationale: Embedding the trailer struct directly in virtnet_info is the core layout mistake: because the trailer contains a flexible array member, tail padding makes its internal hash_key_data offset differ from the separately stored RSS key buffer, leading to one-byte misaligned access.

This separate buffer placed immediately after the embedded trailer is interpreted as the trailer's flexible-array storage, but due to tail padding in the preceding embedded trailer, accesses via rss_trailer.hash_key_data are off by one relative to this buffer.

vuln_statements.explanation: Embedding struct virtio_net_rss_config_trailer directly inside struct virtnet_info is the layout bug. Because that struct contains a flexible array member, its tail padding makes accesses through rss_trailer.hash_key_data use a different offset than the separately stored RSS key buffer, causing one-byte misaligned reads/writes.

This buffer is placed after the embedded trailer and is effectively treated as backing storage for rss_trailer.hash_key_data. Due to the trailer's tail padding, the flexible-array access lands one byte off relative to this buffer, so this declaration participates directly in the vulnerable layout.

Author: Akihiko Odaki <akihiko.odaki@daynix.com>

    virtio_net: Use new RSS config structs
    
    The new RSS configuration structures allow easily constructing data for
    VIRTIO_NET_CTRL_MQ_RSS_CONFIG as they strictly follow the order of data
    for the command.
    
    Signed-off-by: Akihiko Odaki <akihiko.odaki@daynix.com>
    Acked-by: Jason Wang <jasowang@redhat.com>
    Reviewed-by: Xuan Zhuo <xu
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it shows the full relevant RSS data layout and all accesses/serialization paths. The root cause was embedding `struct virtio_net_rss_config_trailer` with a flexible array member before a separate key buffer, causing `rss_trailer.hash_key_data` and the actual key storage to have different offsets due to tail padding. In this commit, the code no longer relies on an embedded trailer-with-FAM followed by separate storage for command serialization. Instead, `struct virtnet_info` contains `struct virtio_net_rss_config_hdr *rss_hdr;`, `struct virtio_net_rss_config_trailer rss_trailer;`, and `u8 rss_hash_key_data[VIRTIO_NET_RSS_MAX_KEY_SIZE];`, and the command is built using explicit sized scatter-gather buffers: `sg_set_buf(&sgs[0], vi->rss_hdr, virtnet_rss_hdr_size(vi));` and `sg_set_buf(&sgs[1], &vi->rss_trailer, virtnet_rss_trailer_size(vi));`. The size helper `virtnet_rss_trailer_size()` uses `struct_size(&vi->rss_trailer, hash_key_data, vi->rss_key_size)`, so the trailer SG includes the bytes immediately following `rss_trailer` as laid out in `struct virtnet_info`, and the preceding comment/commit message indicates these are the new RSS config structs that strictly follow command order. Also, normal key accesses are done via the separate buffer `vi->rss_hash_key_data` (`netdev_rss_key_fill(vi->rss_hash_key_data, ...)`, `memcpy(rxfh->key, vi->rss_hash_key_data, ...)`, `memcpy(vi->rss_hash_key_data, rxfh->key, ...)`) rather than through a mismatched embedded FAM pointer/offset. This commit is the one described as switching to the new RSS config structs to match the wire format, which is exactly the fix for the offset/padding issue. Therefore the vulnerable construct is not present in this version, and the fix is present.
